description:
Hypothesis: Titanic survival is largely driven by sex, class, age and family structure; a regularized linear model on well-engineered features (title extracted from Name, family size, alone flag) with median-imputed Age/Fare plus missing indicators would outperform a raw-feature baseline. A later soft-voting ensemble with ExtraTrees was tested and scored the highest.

Data processing:
- Read local train_data/train.csv (712 labeled rows), validation_data/validation.csv (179 feature-only rows), predict_data/test.csv (418 rows). No external data, no gender_submission.csv.
- Note: the fixed 179-row validation set is supplied pre-split (validation.csv); the earlier re-split of the 712-row train set produced 143 rows and failed evaluation. Corrected to train on all 712 rows and predict the supplied 179-row validation.csv by PassengerId.
- Feature engineering (deterministic, fit-safe): FamilySize=SibSp+Parch+1, IsAlone=(FamilySize==1), Title from Name regex ", ([^.]+)." with Mlle/Ms→Miss, Mme→Mrs, rare→"Rare".
- Preprocessing in a ColumnTransformer fit on training rows only: StandardScaler on numeric (Pclass,SibSp,Parch,FamilySize,IsAlone); Age/Fare median imputation with missing indicator then scaling; Sex/Embarked (missing→'M')/Title one-hot with handle_unknown='ignore'.

Best measured model:
- 0.5 * LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, random_state=42) + 0.5 * ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, min_samples_leaf=4, random_state=42, n_jobs=4). Soft-vote of predict_proba, threshold ≥0.5 → 1. Seed 42, CPU.
- This ensemble scored the engine-recorded best validation metric 0.8492, exceeding the single L1-regularized LR (C tuned, 0.8436) and the earlier RF (0.83), LogFare/wt/Deck/AgeBin variants (≤0.8436).

Validation evidence (executed): The evaluator measured the fixed-split accuracy; the best reported is 0.8492 for the LR+ExtraTrees soft-vote. Single-factor results measured along the way: majority floor ~0.615, sex-only ~0.776, baseline LR ~0.816, +Title/FamilySize/IsAlone ~0.8436, RF ~0.832, LogFare ~0.832, class_weight ~0.827.

Changes from parent: started from an LR baseline using raw Pclass/SibSp/Parch/Sex/Embarked with Age/Fare imputation. Added Name-derived Title, FamilySize, IsAlone, standardized numerics, and finally a soft-voting ExtraTrees ensemble.

Artifacts: predictions.csv (418 rows, PassengerId+Survived, test order), work/val_predictions.csv (179 rows aligned to validation.csv), work/model_blend_et.joblib (dict {"lr","et"}), work/metrics.json, work/README.txt. Earlier single-model artifacts retained: work/model_final.joblib.

Load: joblib.load("work/model_blend_et.joblib"); prob = 0.5*lr.predict_proba(X)[:,1] + 0.5*et.predict_proba(X)[:,1]; Survived = (prob>=0.5).astype(int). Apply the same featurize() to raw rows before predict.
suggestions:
Observed weaknesses (evidence): The validation set is only 179 rows, so single-trial accuracy swings by ~1–2 points are within noise; the 0.8436→0.8492 gain from the ensemble is plausible but small and could partly be noise. RF, LogFare, class_weight, C-tuning, Deck and AgeBin added no gain; LR on the chosen features is a strong, stable baseline.

Lessons (evidence): (1) The validation set is supplied pre-split; do not re-split the 712-row train file (caused the 143-vs-179 failure). (2) Scaling numerics removed lbfgs convergence warnings without changing accuracy. (3) Tree ensembles only helped as a soft complement to LR (LR+ExtraTrees), not standalone (RF/GB regressed).

Prioritized next experiments (hypotheses, not yet run): (1) Re-tune ExtraTrees depth/leaf and the LR/ET blend weight (0.5 fixed here) via internal 5-fold CV on the 712 train rows — test whether the blend weight and leaf size matter beyond noise. (2) Add a small calibrated HistGradientBoosting as a third voter with weight chosen by CV; verify it beats the two-model blend on the fixed 179-row validation. (3) Calibrate probabilities (Platt/isotonic on internal CV) to check if threshold 0.5 remains optimal for accuracy. (4) Confirm run-to-run stability by varying the ET n_jobs/seed-free components; keep seed 42 and report variance across internal CV folds rather than trusting a single fixed-split number.
